elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Licensor may request such an audit no more than once in any 12-month period" — replaces the original unlimited request right and caps frequency.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "on at least 30 days' prior written notice to Licensee"; the original sentence giving Licensee 30 days to permit an audit after a request (a compliance deadline, not advance notice) was replaced, so no contradictory timing survives.
Inserted: "Each such audit shall be conducted during Licensee's normal business hours".

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Retained original: "Licensee agrees to allow an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement) to audit"; the new sentence's reference to "an auditor" does not displace the retained independence requirement.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "by an auditor bound by confidentiality obligations".

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained unchanged: "The cost of the audit will be borne by Licensor unless a discrepancy of more than five-percent (5%) is discovered, in which case the cost of the audit shall be borne by Licensee." Licensor (Vendor) is the default cost bearer with a 5% shift threshold.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "and Licensor shall have no direct access to Licensee's systems"; the audit scope otherwise remains limited to accounting records.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: "no more than once in any 12-month period" satisfies a once-per-year cap.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: "at least 30 days' prior written notice" exceeds the 15-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: The retained cost clause shifts cost to Licensee at a discrepancy over 5%, so between 5% and 10% Customer bears cost; literally short of the 10% fallback trigger, though this is the playbook's own preferred 5% formulation and the preferred element is met.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element; noted only for completeness — retained 5% threshold satisfies the preferred cost element.

reasons: All eight preferred elements are met in operative language: frequency cap and 30-day prior written notice in the replacement sentence; business hours, off-site-where-possible, auditor confidentiality and no-system-access in the added sentence; independent CPA/Audit Professional and the Licensor-cost/5%-discrepancy allocation retained unchanged.
The position is complete at the preferred level, so the fallback shortfall (5% rather than 10% cost-shift threshold, which is the playbook's own preferred formulation) is immaterial.

Minimality holds: the only deletion is the original sentence "Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.", which is inside the notice/frequency target and would otherwise contradict the new 30-day prior-notice requirement. No survival tails, expense allocations, procedures or extra requirements outside the checklist were added.

Intent is preserved: the audit remains limited to accounting records for compliance verification, the mutual-agreement auditor selection and the Licensor-borne cost/5% shift mechanic survive intact, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.
Finding status "deviation" is correct: the original clause was unlimited in frequency with no advance notice, which is walk-away territory under the rule.
